label: Base-lock v1 combined recorded list on the resident arm A (4 x TP2, -v2 profile, ceiling 32): R0 once, then R-A2-L32 (normal mix at the admitted knee 32, 3 passes), R-A3-L32 (worst case at 32, min_tokens 4096, admissibility) and R-A3-b6144 (worst case at the raised 7168-token cap, levels 32, 24, 16, thinking budget 6144). Whole list on_fail stop_chain (planner ruling 2026-10-30). Synthetic prompts only; no dataset row.

runs.note: normal mix at the admitted knee 32 per instance at 3x requests (the example list's R-A2 restricted to 32)
worst case at 32 with every completion forced to 4096 tokens; zero preemptions on every instance and KV peak <= 90 % (the example list's R-A3)

worst case at the 7168-token cap in descent order; on_fail continue so 32, 24 and 16 are all measured; admitted_level 32 is only the upper bound the validator needs (rule (b)) and is left for the planner to lower; the planner reads worst_case_admissible and the per-instance preemption and KV-peak columns per level. The plan 3.4 max-latency threshold scales with the output cap: 420 s bounds 4096 tokens at about 9.8 tok/s, so the same floor at 7168 tokens is 735 s (= the fragment timeout_seconds); the p10 e2e floor of 10 tok/s is unchanged. prompt_max 17408 = 24576 - 7168 (the sweep preflight refuses more); sweep timeout 800 s is above the 735 s latency rule so a slow request is a latency failure, not a client timeout. In this combined list on_fail is stop_chain (planner ruling), so a failing level ends the chain and the lower levels are not measured.
